name: Global Talent visa

requirements.blocker_text: Endorsement is only available in academia/research, arts and culture, or digital technology.

This requires a formal endorsement from the body matching your field — Royal Society, British Academy, Royal Academy of Engineering, or UKRI for academia/research; Arts Council England for arts and culture; Tech Nation for digital technology. This is a discretionary, evidence-based decision, not a checkable personal attribute.
requirements.fix_path: Build an evidence portfolio against the specific endorsing body's published criteria and submit the Stage 1 endorsement application. This is the actual barrier — most unsuccessful applications fail here, not at the visa stage.

requirement_groups.name: Named winner of a prestigious prize

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being the named winner of a specific prize on the Home Office's published Global Talent prize list — other prizes from the same institution do not count.

evidence_required.document: Evidence portfolio against the endorsing body's published criteria (track record, letters of recommendation, evidence of impact)
Reference letters from established figures in the applicant's field
Proof of named prize win (prize route only)

outcome.duration_length: up to 5 years, freely chosen at each renewal, no cap on total time before settling

notes: SCHEMA GAP PARTIALLY FIXED (2026-08-08): pr_after_months/citizenship_after_months now correctly vary by group via outcome_override — prestigious_prize uses 36/48 months (matches route-level default), endorsement uses 60/72 months. This resolves the original ambiguity where a single route-level Outcome couldn't express both real figures. REMAINING GAP, flagged honestly rather than hidden: the 'endorsement' group itself still conflates two real internal tiers — Exceptional Talent (established leader, faster path) and Exceptional Promise (emerging leader, common in digital technology and arts and culture, slower path) — which the endorsing body assigns as a discretionary outcome of the SAME application, not something the applicant can select in advance as a separate RequirementGroup. The 60-month figure encoded here is the Exceptional Promise figure, the more common and more conservative assumption; Exceptional Talent endorsees could reach PR in as little as 36 months, same as the prize route. A fully accurate model would need a third pseudo-group or a qualifying_event-level distinction most applicants can't self-assess before applying — deliberately not forced in, since fabricating a selectable predicate the applicant can't actually test against would be worse than the current honest approximation. No sponsor, no salary threshold, no job offer required at any stage — the most unrestricted work route in this dataset, traded against the hardest evidential bar to clear. Fee sources conflict sharply online: several 2026 guides cite £816 or an older £524+£623 split; gov.uk confirms £766 total, current as of the 3 August 2026 page update — flagged as a live counterfeit-figure case alongside the UK Skilled Worker salary discrepancy.
